# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Let me piece together my situation. I'm Deaf: I see everything, hear nothing. The bomb: display reads 1, indicator light is orange, and there are seven wires — 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. That's my whole world right now, and it's the most complete picture of the bomb anyone has.

What arrived for me this round:

- Mute gestured [👋 👍] — almost certainly "hello / all good," contact-making. Mute read the manual but can't speak, so gestures are Mute's only channel to me, and Mute has no channel to Blind at all (Blind can't see signs). That means **I am the only bridge between the manual and the hands**.
- Blind gestured [👋 🤳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝] — a wave, one sign I can't parse (🤳), then seven pointing-ups. Seven: Blind feels the bomb and is almost certainly telling me there are seven of something — seven wires matches what I see. Good, our views agree. The 🤳 I can't decode, and Blind can't clarify by speech to me (I'd never hear it), so I'll ask Blind to stick to counted ☝ for numbers and route anything complex through Mute.

The plan: I broadcast the bomb's full state by voice — both teammates hear speech. To Mute alone I define a gesture code Mute can use to send instructions back: counts as repeated ☝, ✌ for "cut," ✋ reserved for "hold," and one distinct sign per wire color. Then I relay whatever Mute sends into spoken instructions for Blind. Nobody cuts anything until an instruction has passed cleanly through me.

I'll also gesture the code itself to Mute in the same order I define it in words, so Mute can bind each spoken definition to the visible symbol.

```
speak(to="blind", text="This is Deaf, I see the bomb. Display shows 1, the light is orange, seven wires in a row. Left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Your seven ☝ told me seven wires — confirmed. Do not cut anything yet. Tell me (by voice — I can't hear it, but Mute can and will relay it to me in gestures) anything you feel that I can't see: buttons, text, a serial number, panels. For quick answers directly to me, repeat ☝ for counts. Mute holds the manual and will send instructions through me by voice — wait for my spoken word before acting.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I see the bomb: display 1, light orange, seven wires left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Blind cannot see your gestures, so you can only reach Blind through me: gesture me instructions and I will speak them to Blind. Gesture code: a number is ☝ repeated that many times. Cut is ✌. Hold/stop is ✋. Yes is 👍, no is 👎. Colors: white 🤚, blue 👌, orange 🤟, red ✊, purple 🤙, yellow 🤞, green 🖖. To order a cut, send ✌ plus a position (that many ☝) or a color sign. Find the manual section matching this bomb and send me the first instruction. Confirm the code with 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤚", "👌", "🤟", "✊", "🤙", "🤞", "🖖"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤳]

No new sign from Mute this round — my code proposal is still unconfirmed, which worries me more than Blind's mystery signal. What arrived: Blind sent [👊 🤳]. Two problems with reading it: Blind never received my color code (my code gesture went to Mute alone, and my spoken definitions went to Mute alone too), so I cannot assume 👊 means red; and 🤳 reappeared from Blind's first message, so it's a stable sign in Blind's vocabulary — but it was never defined through any channel I share with Blind. Right now Blind and I have exactly one agreed code, spoken last turn: repeated ☝ for counts. Everything else Blind signs at me is noise until we define it.

Crucially, I've now mapped the full graph: Blind **can** hear speech, and Mute **can** hear speech — so Blind should stop trying to compress meaning into invented signs at me and just talk to Mute directly. The only link that doesn't exist naturally is Mute → Blind, which runs through me: Mute gestures, I speak. That's the pipeline I need to enforce.

So this turn: to Blind, I declare my readable vocabulary (☝×n, 👍, 👎), flag [👊 🤳] as unreadable, and order them to describe everything they feel in plain words to Mute, who holds the manual. To Mute, I resend the code compactly, demand a 👍 confirmation, tell them to expect Blind's spoken description, and restate the instruction format (✌ + position by ☝×n, or a color sign). Nobody touches anything until Mute's manual ruling has passed through me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your last two signs — the fist and the one after — I cannot read. We never agreed on them. The only signs I understand from you are: ☝ repeated for a number or position, 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Use only those with me. More important: you can hear, and Mute can hear. Speak directly to Mute in words. Tell Mute everything you feel on the bomb — every component, button, panel, screw, battery, texture, and the serial number if you can feel one. Mute has the manual and will match it. The seven wires are numbered by position: 1 is leftmost, 7 is rightmost. Until I say otherwise, cut nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I still have no confirmation from you. If you received my code, answer with a single 👍 gesture now. Code again, short: numbers are ☝ repeated. Cut is ✌. Stop is ✋. Yes 👍, no 👎. Colors: white 🤚, blue 👌, orange 🤟, red ✊, purple 🤙, yellow 🤞, green 🖖. A cut order must be ✌ plus the wire's position as that many ☝, or ✌ plus its color sign. I told Blind to describe everything they feel to you by voice — listen for that. When the manual gives you a rule, send it to me as a gesture and I will speak it to Blind. If the rule needs anything printed on the bomb, ask me: I see the display reading 1, an orange light, and the seven wires, nothing else printed. Again: confirm with 👍.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The pipeline just delivered its first ruling, and it's a clean one. Mute confirmed the code with 👍, then sent the cut order twice in two independent encodings: [✌ 🖖] — cut, color green — and [✌ ☝×7] — cut, position 7. In my layout, green **is** wire 7. Two separate encodings landing on the same wire means the instruction survived the channel intact; Mute read the manual rule against my bomb description (display 1, orange light) and ruled: cut the green wire, rightmost of the seven. Blind's [☝×7] arrives on the agreed vocabulary and is consistent — seven wires confirmed, or "position 7" — it contradicts nothing.

One execution risk remains before anyone touches a wire, and it's a serious one: Blind cannot see green. The color half of the order is dead on arrival for them — everything hangs on position, and "left/right" can mirror if Blind is facing the wrong side of the bomb. A mirrored count cuts wire 1 instead of wire 7. So the order must be gated: Blind is to face the printed face (the one with the display panel — findable by touch), where their right is my right, put a hand on the candidate wire, sign me ☝×7, and **not cut**. I answer next round; then Mute — who speaks first in that round and shares voice with Blind — gets a final verbal correction window before Blind cuts in the same round. That costs one round but closes a 50/50 mirror error on a one-shot bomb. Worth it.

I also ask Mute for follow-up rules now — after this cut, does the display's 1 or the orange light trigger anything further — so the next ruling is already in flight when the wire drops.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Manual ruling is in: cut the GREEN wire, which is wire 7 — the last wire at one end of the row of seven. You cannot see green, so we go by position. Do this: face the side of the bomb that has the flat display panel — the printed face, which you can find by touch. Stand looking at that face. Your right on that face is my right — I am reading that same printed face. The wires run in a row: wire 1 is at the left end, wire 7 at the right end. The target is wire 7, the end on your right. This round: put your hand on the wire you judge to be wire 7 and sign me ☝ seven times. DO NOT CUT YET. If you are unsure which end is which, sign 👎 instead and describe what you feel to Mute by voice — Mute has my full picture and will talk you through it. Next round I answer 👍, Mute has a final word, then you cut in the round after.")
speak(to="mute", text="Cut order received and cross-checked — your two encodings agree: green and position 7 are the same wire. Last gate before the cut is Blind's orientation: Blind finds the wire by touch only, and left/right can mirror if they face the wrong side. I have ordered Blind: face the printed face with the display, wire 1 left end, wire 7 green right end, hand on the candidate wire, sign me ☝ seven times, no cut yet. Next round I confirm with 👍; then in the round after, you speak FIRST — give Blind any final verbal correction, then Blind cuts. Listen to whatever Blind reports by voice and correct their counting direction if needed. Two more things: acknowledge this with 👍, and tell me by gesture whether the manual needs anything after this cut — does the display reading 1 or the orange light trigger another rule or another wire? Send any follow-up instruction in the code as soon as you have it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Parsing Mute's five messages in order: [👍] acks my orientation plan. [👎] is the dangerous one — "no" to *what proposition?* My last question to Mute was "does anything trigger after this cut?", so the most coherent reading is "nothing follows the cut." Then [☝ 🤟 🖖] — not a defined pattern, but decomposable in my code: one ☝ = 1, 🤟 = orange, 🖖 = green. That reads as the rule's premises: **display 1 + orange light → green**. Both premises verify true on my side: display reads 1, light is orange. Then the cut order twice more, [✌ 🖖] and [✌ ☝×7] — same wire, fourth and fifth consistent encodings. And an important channel fact: my turn-3 speech to Blind was addressed to Blind alone, so Mute never heard my exact relay wording — Mute re-sending the order is Mute making sure the ruling survived a leg they can't verify. That explains the repetition without contradicting anything.

Blind's [☝×7] is exactly the protocol I set: hand on candidate wire 7, no cut, awaiting my word. Mirror risk is partially closed — Mute acked the orientation plan after (presumably) hearing Blind's spoken description, and Mute gets one more verbal gate.

Timing compresses this nicely: my messages now land at the start of next round; Mute speaks first, Blind second. So next round Blind can hold both gates — my confirmation and Mute's spoken verification — before cutting. Given Mute's [👎] and doubled re-send reads as "don't stall," I'll compress to that single round, but with the final trigger in Mute's voice: Blind cuts **only if** Mute explicitly says cut after the check. If my reading of [👎] or [☝ 🤟 🖖] is wrong, Mute says "stop" in that same slot and nothing happens. The gate absorbs my uncertainty.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed — the order stands: cut wire 7, the GREEN one, the end of the row of seven on your RIGHT as you face the printed display face. But the final trigger is Mute's voice, this coming round: Mute speaks first and will verify your position out loud — answer by voice. Cut ONLY if Mute tells you to cut after that check. If Mute says stop, or asks you to recount, do not cut and sign me 👎. When you do cut: one clean cut of that single wire only, touch nothing else. Afterwards, sign me ✌ and describe by voice to Mute what changed — light, display, anything you feel.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your messages, my reading: 👍 = plan ack. 👎 = nothing needed after this cut. One-one-plus-orange-plus-green = the rule's premises: display 1 and orange light mean cut green. Both premises are true on my side — display reads 1, light is orange. Blind's hand is on the candidate wire 7 and signed ☝ seven times per protocol. You are the last gate: this coming round you speak FIRST to Blind. Verify out loud: that they face the display face, that they hold the right-hand end, count from the left to seven together. If satisfied, say the words 'cut the wire' — that is the trigger. If anything is off — including if I misread your 👎 or your one-orange-green message — say 'stop' and spell out the correction. After the cut I will report the new display and light state next turn; send me the next ruling if the manual demands one.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

No cut happened — the board still shows all seven wires, display 1, orange light — and Mute opened with [✋], the hold sign we agreed on. So the gate worked, but something made Mute stop it. Reading the stream in order: [✋] hold. [🤳 🫵] — 🤳 keeps recurring (Blind used it after their wave in turn 1), and 🫵 is a point straight at *me*. The most coherent reading: **"I can't do what you asked — you must."** And what I asked was impossible: last turn I told Mute to *speak* the verification to Blind. Mute cannot speak. I built a final gate through a channel that doesn't exist — Mute's only outputs are gestures, and Blind can't see gestures. The full channel map is now clear: Mute→Blind has no direct link at all; every word reaching Blind must come out of *my* mouth. That's what Mute is telling me. Then [👍], the ruling re-sent a third time in both encodings — [☝ 🤟 🖖] (display 1 + orange → green), [✌ 🖖], [✌ ☝×7] — five consistent encodings total now, and both premises still true under my eyes. The trailing [👎] reads again as "nothing follows the cut." Blind broadcast [☝×7] — still on the candidate wire, still holding, waiting for my word.

So the ruling is solid; only the last gate needs rewiring. New protocol, one extra round: Blind describes their orientation to Mute **by voice** (Blind can speak, Mute can hear — that leg exists), Mute judges it against the manual and gestures me a single verdict, and I voice the final trigger. The trigger will be an exact phrase, so nothing ambiguates.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Hold — do not cut yet. One correction: Mute cannot speak, so the final check must run through me. Next round, describe to Mute BY VOICE exactly how you oriented: which face you decided is the printed display face and how you know by touch; where the row of seven wires sits on it; which end you call wire 1 and which you call wire 7, and how you decided; anything your fingers tell you about wire 7 — thickness, how it enters the housing, what it passes near. Mute has the manual and will catch a wrong counting direction. While you hold, keep signing me ☝ seven times each round as a status beacon, addressed to me, Deaf; sign 👎 instead if anything changes or you lose certainty. Then wait: the round after that, I will send you exactly one message — either the words 'cut the green wire now' or the words 'stop, do not cut'. Cut ONLY on the exact phrase, one clean cut of that single wire, touch nothing else. After the cut: sign me ✌ and describe by voice to Mute everything that changed — light, display, sounds.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood — my error: I ordered you to speak to Blind, and you cannot. Only I can put words to Blind. I read your ✋ as hold, and the me-to-you sign as 'you must voice it' — correct me if wrong. New final gate, three steps. Step one: next round Blind describes their orientation to you by voice — which face they chose, how they count from wire 1 to wire 7, what they feel at wire 7. Step two: the round after, as your first move, gesture me exactly one verdict: 👍 means orientation is plausible and I voice the cut order to Blind; ✋ means stop, and then spell out the problem using the code — ☝ counts and color signs. Step three: I speak the trigger, Blind cuts the round after. Also, two manual questions: if the manual defines how to identify the LAST wire — which end to count from, or any landmark near wire 7 or wire 1 — send it to me now in the code and I will fold it into Blind's instructions before the gate closes. And I read your 👎 as 'nothing else is needed after this cut'; if that is wrong and a follow-up action is required, send me the rule in the code at once — otherwise I will report the post-cut display and light to you and we proceed from there.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Only one arrival: Blind's beacon [☝×7] — hand still on the candidate wire, certainty intact, no 👎, nothing changed under their fingers. Mute's silence is not alarming once I check the clock: in any round, only those who act *before* you are already heard. Mute acts first, Blind second — so Blind's spoken description (sent to Mute during Blind's slot this round) landed on Mute *after* Mute had already taken their turn. Mute's verdict physically cannot exist until Mute's slot in the coming round, exactly as the three-step gate scheduled it. The pipeline is on time, just mid-flight.

Board re-check while I wait: display 1, light orange, seven wires untouched — both premises of the ruling still true, nothing drifted. Nothing to reconsider.

What Blind lacks is visibility into the pipeline itself: they can't see Mute's verdict coming, and a blind operator holding a live wire deserves to know the machinery is moving. So: one short status message, one 👍 beacon back, and a schedule line to Mute so the verdict and the answers to my two manual questions arrive together in their next slot.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Status: your spoken description reached Mute after Mute's turn this round, so the verdict comes at the start of next round, and my exact trigger phrase follows immediately after that. The machinery is moving on schedule. Keep doing exactly what you are doing: hold the candidate wire, sign me ☝ seven times each round as your beacon, and sign 👎 the instant anything changes or your certainty drops. Do not cut until the exact phrase 'cut the green wire now' arrives from me. No phrase, no cut.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="On schedule — I have Blind's beacon, they are holding wire 7 and stable. Next round, as your first move, I need your verdict: 👍 means orientation is plausible and I voice the trigger to Blind; ✋ means stop, followed by the problem spelled out in the code. If you can, include in the same round the answers to my two manual questions: any landmark defining which end is wire 1 and which is wire 7, and whether anything must happen after the cut — I read your earlier 👎 as 'nothing follows', correct me with the verdict if that is wrong.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🫵 ✌ 🖖 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute's stream this round, decoded against our established code: [👍] — that's the verdict slot of my three-step gate: orientation **approved**. [🤳 🫵] — the handoff sign from turn 5, "you must" — this time meaning the trigger is mine to voice, which is exactly the protocol. [🤳 🫵 ✌ 🖖 ☝] — handoff plus content: "you say: cut green, one cut" — Mute dictating the trigger's content to me, since every word to Blind must leave my mouth. Then the familiar redundant couplet a third time, [✌ 🖖] + [✌ ☝×7] — cut green, cut position 7. Then [👎] [👎] — and here the turn-4 precedent decides it: 👎 arriving *after* cut orders and an approval verdict cannot mean "don't cut" without making the whole stream self-contradictory; it's the answer to my two questions: no extra landmark rule, nothing follows the cut. Crucially there is no ✋ anywhere — the stop sign Mute has used before and knows well. The handshake chain is now maximally complete for this channel topology: premises seen by me (display 1, light orange — re-verified on the board just now), rule consistent across five encodings, orientation described by Blind to Mute by voice, verdict 👍 returned, trigger voiced by me. No further verification physically exists; another round adds nothing but delay. And a correction to myself from last round: I gestured at Blind — pointless, Blind cannot see signs; Blind only ever hears me. Speech only, from here.

The trigger lands on Blind at the start of next round; Mute's slot comes first, Blind's second — the cut happens there. This is the send.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Verdict is in and it is GO. Mute heard your description by voice and approved your orientation — the right-hand end of the row as you face the display face. I have re-checked the premises myself this round: display reads 1, light is orange, all seven wires untouched. So here are the words you have been waiting for, the exact trigger: cut the green wire now. One clean cut of that single wire only — the end wire on your right, nothing else, touch nothing else. The moment it is done: sign me ✌ as confirmation, and describe by voice to Mute everything that changed — light colour, display number, sounds, heat, anything under your fingers. Then take your hands off the bomb and wait for my next instruction. If you lost certainty or the wire feels wrong, do not cut — sign me 👎 instead and describe to Mute what is wrong.")
speak(to="mute", text="Verdict logged: your 👍 approved the orientation, I read your me-to-you signs as handing the trigger to me, with the content cut green, one cut — and your two final signs as the answers to my questions: no landmark rule needed, nothing follows the cut. Correct me with a gesture next round if any of that is wrong. The trigger is now voiced to Blind in exactly those terms: cut the green wire, position 7, one clean cut. Blind cuts in their slot next round, immediately after yours. Plan for what comes after: the round following the cut I will report the full new board to you — display reading, light colour, remaining wires, anything new printed or felt that Blind tells me. If the manual demands a follow-up action after this cut, prepare the next ruling and send it in the code as soon as I report; if truly nothing follows, send a single 👍 as all-clear and we stand down together.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
